topic.title: Language-Model Guidance and Explanatory Interfaces
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Language models can be guided through carefully selected hints, structured prompts, external references, or explanations of internal information. This cluster studies interfaces that connect a task or user need with the information a model uses. Some methods change the guidance supplied to a fixed model; others train models to interpret latent activations.
topic.whyItMatters: These interfaces can improve usefulness without always retraining an entire system, but a fluent explanation is not automatically faithful. Evaluation must separate better task performance from accurate reporting of evidence or internal state, especially when guidance is transferred to unfamiliar situations.
topic.evolution: A 2005 story-comprehension model learns which lexical information helps inference. Directional stimulus prompting in 2023 learns instance-specific hints for black-box language models. Recent representatives examine reference-guided decoding and multi-turn adaptation; Activation Oracles in 2026 train language models to answer questions about activations and test generalization across tasks.
openQuestions: When do generated explanations reveal information that actually drives a model’s decision?
How can guidance adapt to users without reinforcing incorrect assumptions?
